newsitem.title: USA: US attache sees Chile softening wheat import rules.
newsitem.headline: US attache sees Chile softening wheat import rules.

text.p: An agricultural attache at the U.S. embassy in Santiago said Chilean officials have recently "let it be known" they intend to change their regulations to permit imports of U.S. wheat from the Pacific Northwest.

In a report drafted Feb. 27 that was released here Tuesday, the attache said the Chilean goverment's intent is to provide a competitive market for its flour millers -- who will soon be negotiating wheat purchases from North America -- without having to rely on the integrity of U.S. quarantine measures.

The attache noted the fungus, which surfaced last year in the U.S. for the first time, prompting a government quarantine of some Southwest and Western states, is reportedly incapable of spreading to northern U.S. wheat producing areas because of climatic conditions.
But the attache forecast Chile wheat imports from United States in 1997 at zero.

"Until Chile publishes its new import regulations stating the precise conditions under which wheat may be imported from the Pacific Northwest, it is impossible to determine whether or not U.S. plant quarantine officials will be willing or able to issue phytosanitary certificates for any Chilean wheat purchases," the report said.
USDA reports are not official USDA data.
